questions.question: Deficit financing means the government borrows money from the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __Reserve Bank of India.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** Deficit financing:

__
 
• Deficit financing means generating funds to finance the deficit which results from an excess of expenditure over revenue.
 
• The gap is covered by borrowing from the public through the sale of bonds or by printing new money.
 
• For developing countries like India, higher economic growth is a priority.
 
• Higher economic growth requires finances.
 
• With the private sector being shy of making a huge expenditure, the responsibility of drawing financial resources rests on the government.
 
• Often both the tax and non-tax revenues fail to mobilize enough resources just through taxes.
 
• The deficit is often funded through borrowings or printing new currency notes.
 
• Deficit financing affects investment adversely.
 
• When there is inflation in the economy employees demand higher wages to survive.
 
• If their demands are accepted it increases the cost of production which de-motivates the investors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__****Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**

__
 
• RBI was established in India on **1st April**, in Kolkata in **1935** under the **Reserve Bank Of India Act, 1934.**
 
• It was set up on the recommendation of the **Hilton Young Commission.**
 
• RBI is the central bank of India and is responsible for the issue and supply of Indian currency.
 
• RBI is the **regulatory body of the Indian Banking system** and it is also managing a countries Payment system.
 
• RBI Headquarters:- **Mumbai.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**World Trade Organization (WTO)

 
• WTO was established in **1995**.
 
• It replaced the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)** that had been established in **1948**. 
 
• WTO is headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland.**

**International Monetary Fund**

 
• International Monetary Fund headquarters is located at **Washington D. C **in the United States. It was founded in **1944**.
 
• International Monetary Fund is an Organization of **190 countries**.
 
• It is working to **secure financial stability, facilitate international trade, promote high employment and economic growth and reduce poverty around the world.**

**Ministry of Finance**

 
• The Ministry of Finance is a ministry within the **Government of India responsible for the country's economy and serves as the Treasury of India.**
 
• It focuses on **taxation**, **financial legislation**, **financial institutions**, **capital markets, central and state finances, and the Union Budget in particular.**

questions.question: Which of the following information is found in Ashoka's inscriptions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All options are correct.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most famous Mauryan ruler was **Ashoka**.
 
• He was the first ruler who tried to take his message to the people through inscriptions.
 
• The information found in Ashoka's inscriptions includes his **life story, internal policy, foreign policy, his religious and moral prospects, Buddhism, and his animal and social welfare program.**
 
• These inscriptions are dispersed throughout the areas of India, Nepal, and Pakistan.
 
• Ashoka's inscriptions are the first tangible evidence of Buddhism.
 
• There are 33 inscriptions in total and primarily classified into the following:
 
 
• Major rock edicts.
 
• Minor rock edicts.
 
• Separate rock edicts. 
 
• Major pillar edicts.
 
• Minor pillar edicts.
 
 
 
• Most of Ashoka’s inscriptions were in Prakrit and were written in the **Brahmi script.**
 
• **Prakrit inscriptions were written in Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts**, which even a commoner could read and understand.
 
• The inscriptions found in the area of Pakistan are in the **Kharoshthi script**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Maurya Dynasty was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BC.
 
• Ashoka was the 3rd ruler of the Dynasty.
 
• Ashoka (273 BC-232 BC):
 
 
• He was the greatest Mauryan ruler, **Governor of Taxila and Ujjain.**
 
• He was the son of **Bindusara**.
 
• Under Ashoka, the Mauryan Empire reached its climax.
 
• Ashoka fought the** Kalinga War in 261 BC.** Later, he was moved by the massacre in this war and, therefore, abandoned the policy of physical occupation in favor of the policy of cultural conquest.
 
• He embraced **Buddhism** under Upagupta.

questions.question: Which part of the Earth has the abundance of nickel and iron?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NIFE.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term ‘NIFE’ refers to the Core of the earth. 
 
• The innermost layer of the Earth is the core, with a radius of about 3500 km.
 
• The core is made up of very heavy material mostly constituted by nickel (Ni) and iron (Fe).
 
• NiFe has an abundance of nickel and iron.
 
• Nife is referred to as Ni – nickel, and Fe – ferrous i.e. iron layer.
 
• The central core has a very high temperature and pressure.
 
• The outer core is in a liquid state while the inner core is in the solid-state.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****SIAL-**

 
• The **uppermost layer** over the earth's surface is called the '**crust**'; It is the thinnest of all the layers and is about 35 km on the continental masses and only 5 km on the ocean floors.
 
• The main mineral constituents of the continental mass are the '**silica** and **alumina**', called '**sial**'.

**SIMA-**

 
• The oceanic crust mainly consists of silica and magnesium, called '**sima**'.
 
• Just beneath the crust is the mantle which extends up to a depth of 2900 km below the crust.

questions.question: Konkan coast is stretched from ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa to Diu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Konkan coast is a** 720 km long coastline that forms and is a rugged section of the western coastline of India.**
 
• It lies between the **Western Ghats and the Arabian sea and extends from the Daman Ganga River to the Terekhol River between Maharashtra and Karnataka.**
 
• Konkan is bound by the **Arabian Sea to the west, the Deccan plateau to the east.**
 
• The Konkan Coast proceeds from the** north at Daman in the Gulf of Khambat extends southwards** all along with the western seaside areas of Maharashtra and Goa and meets the **Canara coast at the northern edge of Karwar District in Karnataka.**
 
• The most well-known islands of Konkan, are **Ilhas de Goa**, the site of the capital city of **Panjim**, and **Salsette Island** on which **Mumbai** is situated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** **Eastern Coastal Plains of India-**

 
• The eastern coastal plains stretch from **West Bengal in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south and pass through Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.**
 
• The Eastern coast is again divided into three categories:
 
 
• **Utkal coast- **Extending between the Chilika Lake and Kolleru Lake, they are much wider than the western coastal plains and undergo immense rainfall.
 
• **Andhra coast- **Extending between the Kolleru Lake and Pulicat Lake, the Andra coast forms a basin area for the Krishna and the Godavari rivers.
 
• **Coromandel coast- **The Coromandel coast extends between **Pulicat Lake and Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu**. This Indian coastline remains dry in summer and receives rainfall during the winters due to the north-east monsoons.
 
 

**Western Coastal Plains of India-**

 
• Western Coastal Plains stretches from Kerala in the south to Gujarat in the north passing through Karnataka, Goa and Maharashtra.
 
• The western coast is further divided into four categories:
 
 
• **Kachchh and Kathiawar coast- **Kachchh, formerly a gulf is formed by the deposition of silt by the Indus. Kathiawar is situated to the south of Kachchh.
 
• **Konkan coast- ** It extends between **Daman in the north to Goa in the south.** Rice and cashew are the two important crops of this region.
 
• **Kanada coast- **It extends between Marmagaon and Mangalore and is rich in iron deposits.
 
• **Malabar coast-** Extending between **Mangalore to Kanyakumari**, the Malabar coast is relatively broad. This region also consists of lagoons running parallel to the coast in southern Kerala.

questions.question: How much water has been allowed to India for irrigation, power generation and transport purposes from Indus river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20%.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indus Waters Treaty was signed on September 19, 1960, by then Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Pakistan's President Ayub Khan.
 
• The treaty was signed with the help of the World Bank, which is also a signatory.
 
• The treaty administers how the river Indus and its tributaries that flow in both countries will be utilized.
 
• According to the treaty, Beas, Ravi, and Sutlej are to be governed by India, while, Indus, Chenab, and Jhelum are to be taken care of by Pakistan.
 
• However, since Indus flows from India, the country is allowed to use 20 percent of its water for irrigation, power generation, and transport purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__****Indus River:**

 
• The river Indus rises in **Tibet, near Lake Mansarovar.**
 
• Flowing west, it enters **India in the Leh.**
 
• Several tributaries, the **Zaskar**, the **Nubra**, the **Shyok**, and the **Hunza**, join it in the Kashmir region.
 
• The Indus flows through Baltistan and Gilgit and emerges from the mountains at Attock.
 
• The Satluj, the **Beas**, the **Ravi**, the **Chenab**, and the **Jhelum** join together to enter the Indus near Mithankot in Pakistan.
 
• Finally, the Indus river drains into the** Arabian Sea.**
 
• Ancient Name: **Sindhu**.
 
• The total length of the Indus River is **3180 km.**

questions.question: The rhythmic contraction of the lining of muscles of canal to push the food along the gut is called ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Peristalsis.**__

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• The rhythmic contraction of the lining of muscles of the canal to push the food along the gut is called peristalsis. The movement comprises of relaxation of circular smooth muscles followed by their contraction behind a chewed material in order to keep it from moving backwards, and then its longitudinal contraction to push the material forward.
 
• The term is derived from the Greek word peristellein, **which means ‘to wrap around’.**
 
• It begins in the oesophagus and helps to move the food along the alimentary canal for the process of digestion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Guttation:**

 
• It​ is the process of loss of water in the form of droplets from the leaf margins or uninjured regions.
 
• It occurs when transpiration is low and water absorption is high i.e. the root pressure is high.
 
• The liquid that is exuded out through guttation contains organic and inorganic dissolved substances along with water, so the liquid is not pure water only.
 
• Guttation is seen in herbaceous plants like tomatoes, grasses, balsam, etc.

questions.question: A body of mass 4 kg accelerates from 15 m/s to 25 m/s in 5 seconds due to the application of a force on it. Calculate the magnitude of this force (in N).
questions.solution:
**__CONCEPT:__**

__
 
• **Force: **Force is a** push or pulls** on an object. A force can cause an **object to accelerate**,** slow down**, **remain in place**, or **change shape.**

Force exerted = mass x acceleration

⇒ F = m × a

Acceleration = (Final velocity - Initial velocity)/time

⇒ a = (v₂ - v₁) / t

Where F is the force exerted on the body, m is the mass of the body, a is the acceleration of the body, v₂ is the final velocity, v₁ is initial velocity and t s time.

**Calculation:__**

**Given data:**

the mass of the body m = 4 kg, Final velocity v₂ = 25 m/s, Initial velocity v₁ = 15 m/s, time t = 5 s.

We know that,

⇒ Acceleration = (Final velocity - Initial velocity)/time

a = (25 - 15)/5 m/s² = 2 m/s²

Also,

⇒ Force exerted = mass x acceleration

⇒ Force = 4 × 2 = **8 N**

 
• So option 2 is correct.

questions.question: During ________ motion of an object along a straight line, the change in velocity of the object for any time interval is zero.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is__** Uniform.**__

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Uniform motion:** The motion of an object in which the object travels in a straight line and its velocity remains constant along that line as it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, irrespective of the duration of the time.
 
• During the uniform motion of an object along a straight line, the change in velocity of the object for any time interval is zero and remains constant with time. In this case, the acceleration would also be equal to zero.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 Uniform Motion
 Non Uniform Motion
 
 

 Average Speed
 The motion is similar to the actual speed of the object.
 The motion is different from the actual speed of the object.
 
 

 Rectilinear Motion
 It has zero acceleration.
 It has non-zero acceleration.
 
 

 Graph
 Distance-time graph shows a straight line
 Distance-time graph shows a curved
 
 

 Distance
 Covers equal distances in an equal time interval.
 Covers unequal distances in equal time

questions.question: The tropical rainforests _______.

options.text: are in the coastal regions only

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **get plenty of rainfall.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Tropical rainforests

 
 
• Tropical rainforests are rainforests that are found in areas in which there is no dry season.
 
• All months have an average precipitation of at least 60 mm.
 
• The Tropical rain forests are roughly located within 28° north or south of the equator, spread in Asia, Australia, Africa, South America, Central America, Mexico, and on many of the Pacific Islands.
 
• Trees that grow above the general canopy, may have heights of 45–55 m, although on occasion a few species will grow to 70–80 m tall.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Montane Forests:**

 
 
• In these types of forests, vegetation varies according to altitude.
 
• They differ significantly along the slopes of the mountain.
 
 
 
• **Mangrove Forests:**- 
 
 
• These are **formed along the banks of river estuaries.**
 
• These are also called **Tidal Forests**.
 
• The mangrove forests of **Sundarbans are the largest mangrove forests in the world.**

questions.question:
Which of the statements given below are correct?

A) Valentino Rossi won the Motorcycle race 2017 Dutch TT MotoGP.

B) United Kingdom hosted the Table Tennis 2017 ITTF Women's World Cup.

C) In 2017, Glenn Maxwell captained the IPL team Kings XI Punjab.
questions.solution:
​The correct answer is __**A and C.**__

• **Glenn Maxwell:-**
 
 
• He is a Right Handed Batsman and Right-arm off-break bowler of the Australian Cricket team.
